fx.basis: Saudi riyal pegged to the US dollar at SAR 3.75 since 1986

governance: Every value is a candidate until a named reviewer approves it through the evidence pipeline's human gate. Low and high are the bounds the sensitivity table uses; base is the proposed HOMER input.

parameters.source_title: SERA consumption tariff table (agricultural above 6,000 kWh/month 22 halala; industrial 20 halala; commercial above 6,000 kWh/month 32 halala)
parameters.basis: Base assumes the farm is metered on the agricultural tariff (aquaculture is licensed by the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture) at the above-6,000 kWh/month rate of 22 halala = SAR 0.22/kWh = USD 0.0587/kWh. Low is the industrial flat rate of 20 halala (USD 0.0533). High is the commercial rate above 6,000 kWh/month, 32 halala (USD 0.0853), in case the connection is classed commercial.
parameters.notes: Tariff category is the single question to confirm with the utility; it moves the grid price by 45 percent between low and high. The SERA page already reflects the May 2025 adjustment for non-residential customers.

parameters.source_title: SERA Small-Scale Solar PV Systems Regulation (net billing, systems 1 kW to 2 MW); export credit reported at 5 halala/kWh for non-residential offtakers, 7 halala/kWh for residential
parameters.basis: Base 5 halala/kWh = USD 0.0133/kWh as the commercial and industrial net-billing credit reported by a Saudi C&I solar developer. Low 0 assumes no export agreement (self-consumption only). High 7 halala/kWh = USD 0.0187/kWh is the residential export rate fixed in the 2020 regulation (https://rise.esmap.org/sites/default/files/library/saudi-arabia/Renewable%20Energy/Kingdom%20of%20Saudi%20Arabia_Regulatory%20Framework%20for%20Small-%20Scale%20Solar%20PV%20Systems.pdf).
parameters.notes: The 2020 regulation left the non-residential export rate to be announced; the 5 halala figure comes from an industry source, not the regulator, so confidence is low. Systems above 2 MW fall outside the small-scale regulation entirely.

parameters.source_title: Saudi Electricity Company FY2024 results presentation, operational KPIs: SAIFI 2.61 (2020), 1.71 (2023), 1.47 (2024) interruptions per customer; 2025 target 0.70
parameters.basis: Base is the 2024 system-average SAIFI. Low is the utility's 2025 target. High is the 2020 value, taken as representative of a weaker rural coastal feeder.
parameters.notes: SAIFI is a system average over all customers; a remote coastal feeder can be worse than the high bound. HOMER draws random outages from this frequency and the mean repair time below.

parameters.source_title: Saudi Electricity Company FY2024 results presentation: SAIDI 112.6 (2020), 92.9 (2023), 79.8 (2024) minutes per customer; SAIDI divided by SAIFI gives the mean interruption duration
parameters.basis: Base 79.8 / 1.47 = 54 minutes = 0.90 h (2024). Low 112.6 / 2.61 = 43 minutes = 0.72 h (2020). High 4 h is a researcher assumption for a storm or transformer failure on a coastal feeder, the event that matters for stock survival.
parameters.notes: The high bound is the reliability case that sizes battery autonomy; it is an assumption, not a measured statistic.

parameters.source_title: Saudi Aramco domestic diesel price: SAR 1.66/L from 1 January 2025 (Arab News), SAR 1.79/L in 2026 (GlobalPetrolPrices, 14 September 2026)
parameters.basis: Base SAR 1.79/L = USD 0.477/L (2026 pump price). Low SAR 1.66/L = USD 0.443/L (2025 price, https://www.arabnews.com/node/2584936/business-economy). High SAR 2.50/L = USD 0.667/L assumes continued cost-reflective reform plus delivery to a remote site; the price rose 44 percent in January 2025 alone.
parameters.notes: Pump price, not delivered price. Aramco reviews diesel annually under the 2022 pricing mechanism.

parameters.source_title: SAMA Inflation Report Q1 2026: repo rate cut to 4.25 percent in December 2025, plus a project risk premium
parameters.basis: Risk-free anchor is the SAMA repo rate of 4.25 percent. Base adds a 375 basis point premium for a private agri-industrial investment (8 percent nominal). Low 6 and high 10 percent bracket the premium.
parameters.notes: HOMER combines this nominal rate with expected inflation to form the real discount rate used in NPC.

parameters.source_title: GASTAT: annual CPI inflation 2.1 percent in December 2025; SAMA Inflation Report Q1 2026 records 1.7 to 1.8 percent in early 2026
parameters.basis: Base 2.0 percent is the 2025 run rate. Low 1.5 reflects early-2026 readings. High 3.0 allows for energy-price reform pass-through.

parameters.source_title: Researcher assumption aligned to PV module warranty life
parameters.basis: 25 years matches the PV lifetime carried on the literature side; 20 years tests a shorter horizon.

parameters.source_title: Team methodology: zero unmet critical load; 1 percent tested only on the total bus
parameters.basis: Aquaculture life support tolerates no planned shortfall, so the base constraint is 0 percent. The 1 percent case exists only to show the cost of the reliability requirement.

parameters.source_title: Researcher assumption: dissolved oxygen in intensive RAS falls to lethal levels within tens of minutes without aeration, so backup must bridge the longest credible outage
parameters.source_url: internal:team literature review, aquaculture load characteristics
parameters.basis: Base 4 h matches the high-bound outage duration; low 2 h and high 8 h bracket the design choice between battery-only and battery-plus-generator backup.
parameters.notes: Used to check storage size, not a HOMER input field.
